documents.title: Refill: atorvastatin
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Atorvastatin 40 mg, 90-day supply requested by pharmacy. Approved, 1 refill. Aspirin is OTC, he buys it himself.

documents.title: Oncology Treatment Summary
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Outside oncology group, summary to PCP.
Dx: small cell lung cancer, extensive stage, malignant R pleural effusion (11/2023).
Treatment: carboplatin/etoposide plus atezolizumab, cycle 1 12/11/2023, 4 cycles completed 3/2024. Now on atezolizumab every 4 weeks as maintenance.
Next restaging in about 3 months.
Allergies: NKDA. Other meds: atorvastatin, aspirin.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Check-in. Finished four rounds of chemo with immunotherapy in March, now getting atezolizumab monthly at the cancer center. Energy coming back slowly, eating fine, lost a few pounds over the winter. Still brings up sputum in the mornings, less on most days; doing the PEP device.

Meds: atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81, plus atezolizumab via oncology.

Exam: thin but well. Clubbing. Crackles at both bases, unchanged. Heart regular, no edema.

A/P
1. ES-SCLC on maintenance immunotherapy, per oncology summary of 4/8.
2. Bronchiectasis, asbestosis: stable.
3. HLD: continue statin.
4. Shingrix #2 today, ok with oncology.
Follow up in the summer, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Appointment Cancelled
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Wife called, infusion got moved to tomorrow and they can't do both. Cancelled 7/23. She'll call back to rebook after his scans.

reports.text: Large circumferential pericardial effusion. Right ventricular diastolic collapse and exaggerated respiratory variation in mitral inflow, consistent with tamponade physiology. Left ventricular systolic function normal by visual estimate. No significant valvular disease.
reports.conclusion: Large pericardial effusion with echocardiographic evidence of cardiac tamponade.

documents.title: Emergency Department Note
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED, 9/14/2024.
SCLC, extensive stage, recurrent R pleural effusion, tapped at the cancer center about a week ago with relief; now short of breath again, coughing, chest pain worse lying flat. No injury.
BP 100/60, HR 110, RR 22, SpO2 92% RA.
JVP up, heart sounds muffled.
Bedside then formal echo: large pericardial effusion, tamponade.
Pericardiocentesis by cardiology, fluid sent; cytology malignant cells.
Admitted. NKDA.
Addendum: R effusion reaccumulated; talc pleurodesis done 9/18 before discharge 9/20.

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with wife after a 6-day stay. Only the brief ED note has come over; history from them.

Timeline per pt: fluid taken off the R lung at the cancer center on 9/6, felt better for a few days, then breathless, coughing, chest pain lying down. ED found a large fluid collection around the heart pressing on it; drained, fluid had cancer cells. While in, the R lung fluid came back and they did a talc procedure to seal it on 9/18.

Now: breathing much better, lying flat again, no chest pain, walking the house without stopping.

Exam: vitals as charted, not tachycardic today. Heart sounds normal, no rub. Reduced sounds R base, crackles both bases as before. No JVD. No edema.

A/P
1. Malignant pericardial effusion with tamponade, drained. Tamponade resolved. Oncology plans to continue atezolizumab, repeat echo per them.
2. Recurrent malignant R pleural effusion, s/p pleurodesis.
3. Return precautions reviewed: breathlessness, chest pain, lightheadedness -> ED.
Requested full discharge summary from hospital.

documents.title: Immunization Visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Flu (high dose) R arm, COVID L arm. Oncology ok'd, timed between infusions. Tolerated. Observed 15 min.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
AWV. Feels he has been holding steady since September. Monthly atezolizumab continues. Morning sputum unchanged. No falls, managing stairs at home slowly. Wife handles appointments.

PHQ-2: 1, feels down some days, no loss of interest; declines counseling for now.
Health care proxy: wife; MOLST discussion started, he wants to think it over with his oncologist.

Vitals stable. Weight 77. Exam: chest as before, heart regular, no edema.

Plan: meds unchanged (atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81). Vaccines up to date this season. Follow up in spring.
